overall_summary: Data shows clear audience preference for domestic relationship dynamics and husband-wife emotional realities ('Shaadi Ke Baad Pyaar Kahan Chala Gaya?', 'पत्नी की ये बात हर पति को समझनी चाहिए'), which heavily outperformed standard poetry or solo motivational shorts. Family and romantic bond themes generate the highest organic reach.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Shaadi Ke Baad Pyaar Kahan Chala Gaya?' (1,766 views) and 'पत्नी की ये बात हर पति को समझनी चाहिए' (1,674 views) significantly outperformed all other content.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more narrative-driven shorts focusing on married life micro-conflicts and unspoken love.

winning_patterns.evidence: Content around mothers ('माँ जब पूछती है...') and fathers ('पापा कभी कहते नहीं...') gained steady views (140-238 views) compared to abstract poetry.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate grounded, everyday family observations into the content pipeline.

weak_patterns.pattern: Abstract or Aggressive Sad Poetry Hooks
weak_patterns.evidence: 'जिस दिन सच लिखूंगा… रिश्तों को षड्यंत्र लिखूंगा 💔' received only 16 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid overly dramatic, poetic, or bitter openings; anchor hooks in relatable, everyday occurrences.

next_video.concept: A husband finding an old forgotten college diary or ticket stub inside his wife's cookbook, realizing how much they used to talk before daily chores took over.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a mundane kitchen scene—tea boiling over while the wife manages two tasks at once.
next_video.twist_direction: The husband stays silent, doesn't complain about the tea, and quietly places a cup on the counter with a sticky note reminding her of who they used to be.
next_video.reason: Matches the proven high-performing husband-wife relationship format while testing a subtler, non-verbal emotional beat.

experiment: Testing a silent, non-verbal expression of care in husband-wife dynamics instead of dialogue-heavy relationship complaints.
